subject: general
question: Tansen, the music legend was a courtier in which of the following courts before coming to Akbar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rewa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tansen** began his illustrious career as a **court musician** in the court of **Raja Ramchandra Singh of Rewa,** also known as **Raja Ramchandra**.
 
• He served as both the court poet and vocalist for Raja Ramchandra Singh before catching the attention of **Emperor Akbar**.
 
• Renowned for his mastery of the **Dhrupad style of singing**, Tansen was not only a vocalist but also an instrumentalist who composed numerous ragas.
 
• During his tenure in the court of Raja Ramchandra Singh, Tansen's musical talents gained widespread acclaim.
 
• Emperor Akbar, upon hearing of Tansen's prodigious abilities, requested his presence at his court through a 'firman' sent to the king.
 
• Tansen was appointed as one of the Navaratnas (Nine Jewels) in Akbar's court, where he was bestowed with the titles of 'Mian' and Kanthabharan Vanivilas.
 
• Tansen quickly became a favorite of Emperor Akbar after joining his court in **1556**.
 
• Legend has it that Tansen's rendition of Raag Deepak was so powerful that it could light even extinguished candles, showcasing the extraordinary depth of his musical talent and influence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abu'l-Fath Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Akbar,** popularly known as **Akbar the Great, **or Akbar I, was the **third Mughal emperor**, reigning from **1556 to 1605.**
 
• Following the reign of his father, Humayun, Akbar ascended to the throne under the **regency of Bairam Khan, **who played a pivotal role in expanding and consolidating Mughal territories in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• During Akbar's rule, Mughal India experienced significant economic growth and stability. The empire's economy tripled in size and wealth, fostering commercial expansion and promoting the flourishing of an Indo-Persian culture.
 
• Akbar's reign is characterized by his efforts to create a strong and prosperous empire, marked by administrative reforms, religious tolerance, and cultural patronage.
 
• After his death in 1605, Akbar was succeeded as emperor by his son, Prince Salim, who later became known as Jahangir.
